discussion_comments.comment_body: AI Review: This selected state sets the button's active-selection foreground, but `.sidebar-migration-count` still directly sets `descriptionForeground`, so the count does not inherit it. With the default light tokens that is about 1.25:1 contrast on the active-selection background. Add a selected descendant rule such as `.sidebar-migration-button.selected .sidebar-migration-count { color: inherit; }`.

🤖 **[P3] This adds a `:has()` selector despite the repository's explicit CSS rule against descendant-state selectors.** The PR also adds several non-focus `!important` declarations to fight `.monaco-button` defaults. Please put a stable marker class on the owned fact-value node and resolve the button cascade through scoped specificity rather than `:has()`/`!important`.

Partially current, but still helpful. The :has() portion had already been replaced by a stable has-actions marker on the latest head, while several non-focus !important overrides remained. I removed the remaining PR-added non-focus !important declarations and configured the owning Button instances/styles so the cascade no longer needs them. For better precision on a moving PR, the bot should separate :has() and !important into distinct findings and re-check each selector against the latest head before posting; combining them made half of the thread outdated while the other half remained valid.
